rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses seeks assistance to help him persist in obedience.
rows.anchor: وطلب المعاونة حرصا على القيام بالطاعة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The alleged sin against Pharaoh's people was Moses' killing of the Egyptian.
rows.anchor: دعوى ذنب وهو قتل القبطي، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's answer, “No,” means events will not unfold as Moses fears: they will not kill him, and he will be safe.
rows.anchor: كلا يعني لا يكون كما ظننت، ولا يقتلونك وأنت آمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to go addresses Moses and Aaron, and the signs are proofs.
rows.anchor: فاذهبا يعني موسى وهارون بآياتنا بحججنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being with them as a hearer means listening in a way that aids and protects them.
rows.anchor: إنا معكم مستمعون سماع من يعينك ويحفظك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God hears what Moses and Aaron say and what their opponents reply; the assurance strengthens their hearts.
rows.anchor: سامعون لما تقولون وما يجيب أولئك، وأراد تقوية قلبيهما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The phrase may simply mean that God is listening.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه إنا مستمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural form “listeners” can be used for glorification.
rows.anchor: من جهة الجمع، وإنما ذكر للتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Listening” can mean “hearing,” since istimāʿ is seeking to hear.
rows.anchor: مستمعا بمعنى سامع؛ لأن الاستماع طلب السماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks Pharaoh to send the Israelites with him, without enslaving or killing them.
rows.anchor: أن أرسل معنا بني إسرائيل ولا تستعبدهم ولا تقتلهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says Pharaoh had enslaved the Israelites for four hundred years.
rows.anchor: قيل: كان استعبدهم أربعمائة سنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report gives a shorter period of enslavement without specifying its length.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أقل، وفي الكلام حذف كأنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording omits the journey and delivery of the message: go to Pharaoh in Egypt and convey it.
rows.anchor: فانطلقا إلى فرعون بمصر، وبلغا الرسالة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Moses and Aaron reportedly waited at Pharaoh's door for a year before he admitted them and they delivered the message.
rows.anchor: بقيا على بابه سنة حتى أذن لهما وأديا الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh recognized Moses and asked whether he was the child they had raised, phrasing the question as a reproachful reminder.
rows.anchor: فلما نظر إلى موسى عرفه، فقال له على وجه الاستفهام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view is that Pharaoh mentioned raising Moses to display his favor to him.
rows.anchor: قيل: قاله إظهارا لنعمته عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view is that Pharaoh invoked Moses' upbringing to deny his prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل قاله إنكارا لرسالته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further possibility is that Pharaoh asked to establish whether Moses really was the same person.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أنه سأله ليعلم أهو هو على الحقيقة أم لا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Moses reportedly lived among Pharaoh's people for thirty years.
rows.anchor: ولبثت فينا من عمرك سنين) قيل: ثلاثون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deed Pharaoh mentions was Moses' killing of the Egyptian.
rows.anchor: وفعلت فعلتك التي فعلت) يعني قتل القبطي

rows.speaker: الحسن والسدي
rows.claim: “Among the disbelievers” means disbelieving in the religion Pharaoh's people followed, which Pharaoh uses to blame Moses.
rows.anchor: من الكافرين بالدين الذي نحن عليه فتعيبه، عن الحسن، والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد وأبو علي
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that Pharaoh meant Moses was ungrateful for Pharaoh's favor and upbringing.
rows.anchor: من الكافرين لنعمتي وحق تربيتي، عن ابن عباس، وابن زيد، وأبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh may have echoed a statement he heard from Moses denouncing him and his people as disbelievers.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أنه اتبع في تسمية موسى بالكفر كلاما سمعه من موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says he acted while astray from revealed law, having no guidance from scripture or religious law.
rows.anchor: من السنن والوحي والشرع، فلم أهتد إلى شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: “Astray” can mean that Moses missed the right course.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الضالين عن طريق الصواب

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Another view is that Moses did not know the killing would lead to his own death.
rows.anchor: عن العلم أن ذلك يؤدي إلى قتله، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Flight and escape are synonymous terms; gift, connection, and donation are likewise synonyms.
rows.anchor: الفرار والهرب من النظائر، والهبة والصلة والعطية من النظائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gift is a legally valid contract by offer and acceptance according to consensus.
rows.anchor: الهبة: عقد جائز في الشرع صحتها بالإيجاب والقبول بالاتفاق

rows.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء
rows.claim: Most jurists require taking possession and delivery for a gift to become valid.
rows.anchor: قيل: بالقبض والتسليم عند أكثر الفقهاء

rows.speaker: الهادي
rows.claim: Al-Hadi holds that a gift is valid without possession.
rows.anchor: وقال الهادي: تصح من غير قبض

rows.speaker: أهل العراق
rows.claim: The Iraqi jurists do not permit gifting an undivided share when the property is divisible.
rows.anchor: فلا يجوز في المشاع فيما ينقسم عند أهل العراق

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi holds that such a gift is valid.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي: تصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿbīd means making a person a slave; the verb has the forms ʿabadtuhu and aʿbadtu-hu.
rows.anchor: والتعبيد: اتخاذ الإنسان عبدا، يقال: عبدته وأعبدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A madman is one whose reason is covered by illness; the root denotes covering, as in night covering someone and the words for jinn and garden.
rows.anchor: المجنون: الذي غطت العلة عقله، وأصله الستر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubīn means manifest or made manifest; the root concerns cutting or becoming distinct.
rows.anchor: والمبين: المستبين، أبان الشيء يبين إبانة إذا استبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “an ʿabbadta,” the accusative can remove an implied preposition, meaning by your enslaving or because you enslaved them.
rows.anchor: النصب بنزع الخافض أي: بتعبيدك أو لتعبيدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is nominative as an apposition to favor: “the favor of your enslaving.”
rows.anchor: الرفع على البدل من النعمة، تقديره: وتلك نعمة تعبيدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses fled to Midian because he feared Pharaoh's people would kill him over the Egyptian he struck.
rows.anchor: ففررت منكم إلى مدين لما خفتكم على نفسي من القتل بالقبطي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Moses feared their reaction to his religious dissent and aid to the Israelites.
rows.anchor: خفتكم لما ظهر مني من مخالفتكم في الدين وإعانتي بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view denies retaliation because Moses acted mistakenly.
rows.anchor: قيل: لم يكن عليه قصاص؛ لأنه مخطئ

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second view denies retaliation because the Egyptian's blood was licit.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه مباح الدم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third view says retaliation was a legal institution not yet established, so Moses feared oppression and transgression.
rows.anchor: القصاص أمر شرعي؛ ولم يكن ثم شرع، وإنما خاف منهم الظلم والتعدي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Ḥukm means knowledge and understanding; the author prefers this because it is paired with messengerhood.
rows.anchor: قيل: علما وفهما؛ وهو الأولى؛ لأنه عطفه على الرسالة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation of ḥukm is prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being made one of the messengers means being included among the prophets.
rows.anchor: وجعلني من المرسلين أي: من جملة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported interpretation treats Moses' response as acknowledging a favor.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنه اعتراف بالنعمة من موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses fled before his prophethood, became a prophet after leaving Egypt, and struck the Egyptian before prophethood.
rows.anchor: أن فراره كان قبل النبوة، وأن نبوته كانت بعد خروجه من مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “my Lord gave me” knowledge shows that all knowledge comes from God: necessary knowledge is created by Him; acquired knowledge follows His proofs, reason, and prompting; revealed knowledge comes by His revelation.
rows.anchor: فإذا جميع العلوم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exchange shows that God is known through His acts, which is why Moses answers by describing them.
rows.anchor: يعرف بأفعاله لذلك اقتصر في الجواب عليه ولم يعدل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response rejects likeness to created things: if God were a body, something could resemble Him and He could be pointed to.
rows.anchor: تدل على نفي التشبيه؛ إذ لو كان جسما لشبهه شيء ولكان يشير إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses show Pharaoh called his people to take him as a deity and worship him.
rows.anchor: أن فرعون كان يدعو قومه إلى أن يتخذوه إلها يعبدونه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Pharaoh commanded worship of himself and the idols he set up, while claiming to be the highest lord.
rows.anchor: كان يأمرهم بعبادته وبعبادة الأصنام بنصبها، ويقول: أنا ربكم الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obeying and following another's religion without God's permission amounts to taking that person as a deity: Pharaoh's followers knew he was no creator but treated his commands as religious law.
rows.anchor: فكانوا يحلون ما أحل، ويحرمون ما حرم، ويتبعونه فيما أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the Israelites inherited the spoils shows they could receive war booty; if the report is sound, it refers to captives.
rows.anchor: أن الغنائم كانت تحل لبني إسرائيل، والخبر إن صح محمول على الأسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story demonstrates God's wise planning and a true prophet's miracle: believers crossed a dry path safely while the unbelievers drowned.
rows.anchor: نجى المؤمنين في طريق يبس، وغرق فيها أولئك الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account consoles the Prophet because most people do not believe.
rows.anchor: تسلية للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بما بين أن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage attributes failure to believe to people's own actions.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن ترك الإيمان فعلهم

rows.speaker: قراءة العامة
rows.claim: The common reading has yasmaʿūnakum with fatḥa on yāʾ and mīm.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: (يسمعونكم) بفتح الياء والميم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read yasmaʿūnakum with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on mīm.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم بضم الياء وكسر الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception “except the Lord of the worlds” applies to all the objects of worship previously mentioned.
rows.anchor: استثناء من جميع المعبودين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ʿaduww functions like a verbal noun, it does not take dual or plural forms, as with khasm and ʿadl.
rows.anchor: وقع موقع المصدر فلا يثنى ولا يجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes ʿaduww distributively: each idol is an enemy.
rows.anchor: معناه كل واحد منهم عدو

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ calls the wording an inversion, meaning that Abraham is an enemy to them.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء هو من المقلوب، أراد: فإني عدو لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb is accusative by exception, as though Abraham said, “I worship the Lord of the worlds.”
rows.anchor: نصب رب بالاستثناء كأنه قيل: أعبد رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, illā means “but.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلا بمعنى (لكن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “la-fī ḍalālin” is the lām of initiation in the predicate of a softened inna, distinguishing it from inna of negation.
rows.anchor: لام الابتداء التي تدخل في خبر (إن) و(إن) هذه المخففة من الثقيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fanakūna is subjunctive because it answers the wish with fā; when fā is no longer connective, an is understood.
rows.anchor: ونصب (فنكون) لأنه جواب التمني بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ is omitted from yahdīn and yasqīn as it is at the end of poetic lines.
rows.anchor: (يهدين) حذفت الياء كما تحذف من القوافي، وكذلك يسقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs is indeclinable because it is a foreign name.
rows.anchor: إبليس لا ينصرف؛ لأنه اسم أعجمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajmaʿūn is an adjective modifying the troops.
rows.anchor: أجمعون من نعت الجنود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Abraham narrative follows Moses' story to console the Prophet, promise him victory, and warn his people.
rows.anchor: قصة [موسى - عليهما السلام - تسلية] لرسوله فيما لقي من قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabaʾ Ibrāhīm means Abraham's account, and his father is identified as Āzar.
rows.anchor: نبأ إبراهيم أي: خبره إذ قال لأبيه آزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀkifīn means continually remaining and adhering to the idols.
rows.anchor: أي: لا نزال مقيمين على عبادتها ملازمين لها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains ʿākifīn as people praying to the idols.
rows.anchor: عاكفين: مصلين، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they worshipped the idols by day, not at night.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما قالوا ذلك لأنهم كانوا يعبدونها بالنهار دون الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idol worship persists through imitation of parents and leaders, upbringing, and familiarity; this explains most worshippers.
rows.anchor: تقليد الآباء والرؤساء والنشوء عليه والإلف له، وعلى هذا أكثرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many Arabs imagine idols bring them nearer to God as intermediaries, like kissing a king's carpet to approach him.
rows.anchor: توهم قوم أنها تقربهم إلى الله زلفى، فجعلوها واسطة بينهم وبين الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another rationale links worship of God to a visible image.
rows.anchor: ومنها: ارتباط عبادة الله بصورة ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that each people has its own particular reason for worshipping an idol.
rows.anchor: ومنها: لكل قوم خاصية في عبادة الصنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's questions are a rebuke: idols are lifeless things that cannot hear prayer, benefit, or harm their worshippers.
rows.anchor: وهذا استفهام والمراد الإنكار بالإشارة إلى أنها ليست بحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason condemns worship of something inert, since worship is warranted by benefaction and deserving divinity.
rows.anchor: وعبادة مثل هذا تقبح في العقل؛ لأن العبادة تحسن لأجل فعل النعم واستحقاقها بالإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By citing their fathers, the people admit that idols neither hear nor benefit nor harm; they follow custom rather than argument.
rows.anchor: وبينوا أنهم سلكوا في عبادتها طريقة التقليد لا طريقة الحجاج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The idols are Abraham's enemies on the Day of Resurrection if he worships them in this life.
rows.anchor: عدو لي يوم القيامة إن عبدتهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Calling the idols enemies can mean that enmity toward the worshipped objects is enmity toward their worshippers.
rows.anchor: أراد بالعداوة عداوة عبادها، فإن من عادى المعبود فقد عادى عبدته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes “enmity” to mean disavowal.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالعداوة البراءة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: If the idols were alive and invited people to worship them, they would deserve enmity; calling them enemies is figurative.
rows.anchor: فسماه عدوا مجازا، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the phrase as meaning that Abraham is an enemy to the idols.
rows.anchor: معناه أنا عدو لهم، عن الفراء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The phrase need not mean enmity; it can mean that the idols are unfit for worship.
rows.anchor: لم يرد العداوة ولكن أخبر أنهم لا يصلحون للعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may parallel the description that they will be opponents to their worshippers, as a reproach.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه كقوله: (ويكونون عليهم ضدا) والمراد التوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham excludes the Lord of the worlds because He alone is the God Abraham loves to worship and does worship.
rows.anchor: فإنه معبودي الذي أحب عبادته وأعبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham describes God as possessing complete power and abundant blessings, and therefore as the one who deserves worship.
rows.anchor: بما يدل على كمال قدرته وسبوغ نعمه وأنه سبحانه المستحق للعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's creation of Abraham is followed by guidance because guidance completes all blessings.
rows.anchor: لأن جميع النعم تتم بالهداية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Guidance can mean directing Abraham to the path of goodness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يدلني على سبيل الخير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is guidance to Paradise: God charges Abraham with worship here and guides him to Paradise hereafter.
rows.anchor: إلى الجنة، كلفني في الدنيا بعبادته ويهديني في الآخرة إلى جنته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Guidance can also mean that God supports Abraham through His gracious aid.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يؤيدني بألطافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham attributes illness to himself because that is ordinary Arabic usage; he attributes healing to God.
rows.anchor: فأضاف المرض إلى نفسه؛ لأن أهل اللغة يقولون: مرض فلان، فيضاف إليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: He may attribute illness to himself out of good manners because his people regarded it as a defect.
rows.anchor: لأن قومه كانوا يعدونه عيبا فاستعمل حسن الأدب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation says that God heals illness caused by sins through repentance.
rows.anchor: إذا مرض بالذنوب شفاني بالتوبة، عن الصادق

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq reports that when Abraham is ill through sins, God heals him by repentance.
rows.anchor: شفاني بالتوبة، عن الصادق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's causing Abraham to die and then live means He postpones him until recompense.
rows.anchor: ليؤجلني إلى الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṭmaʿu means “I hope”; Abraham's hope is certain, but its wording is a tactful way to ask for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: أرجو، وهذا طمع يقين، وإنما ذكر الطمع تلطفا في الاستدعاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Khaṭīʾatī means minor sins; asking forgiveness is permissible even when they are forgiven, as an expression of reliance and renewed repentance.
rows.anchor: قيل: الصغائر، وهي وإن وقعت مغفورة فيجوز طلب المغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for forgiveness serves four purposes: admitting fault, relying on God, worshipping, and repairing a shortfall in reward.
rows.anchor: أولها: الاعتراف بالخطأ. والثاني: الانقطاع إلى الله. والثالث: التعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The minor sins Abraham sought forgiveness for may be unspecified, since no accountable person is entirely free of them.
rows.anchor: إنها غير معينة ولا يعرى المكلف من ذلك

rows.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Muqātil identify the sin as Abraham's statement, “I am sick.”
rows.anchor: هي قوله: (إني سقيم) عن مجاهد، ومقاتل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view names Abraham's statement that the largest idol did it, his calling Sarah his sister, and his saying of the stars, “This is my lord.”
rows.anchor: بل قوله: (بل فعله كبيرهم) وقوله لسارة: هي أختي، وللكواكب: هذا ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects those proposed sins: he has interpreted the relevant passages elsewhere, and none is a lie or sin.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح شيء من ذلك، وقد بينا تأويل الآيات في مواضعها

rows.speaker: حمزة وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read atawhu with a short alif and fatḥa on tāʾ, a past-tense form meaning that they came to Him; the reading is also attributed to a group and Ibn Masʿūd.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة وحفص عن عاصم: (وكل أتوه داخرين) مقصورة الألف غير ممدودة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: The other reading lengthens the alif and has ḍamma on tāʾ, making it an active participle for the plural subject; it is also attributed to ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: قرأ الباقون: آتوه بمد الألف وضم التاء، وهو قراءة علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read khabīr bimā yafʿalūn in the third person; Abū ʿUbayd prefers it because atawhu reports what they did.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم ويعقوب: خبير بما تفعلون بالياء على الكناية

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use the second-person address in khabīr bimā tafʿalūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالتاء على الخطاب

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read faziʿ with tanwīn and yawmaʾidh with fatḥa on mīm; Ibn Masʿūd shares this reading.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: فزع منونة، يومئذ بفتح الميم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع
rows.claim: They read faziʿ without tanwīn as a genitive construction and yawmaʾidh with fatḥa on mīm.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع: فزع غير منونة على الإضافة يومئذ بفتح الميم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read faziʿ without tanwīn as a genitive construction and yawmaʾidh with kasra on mīm.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: فزع بغير تنوين على الإضافة يومئذ بكسر الميم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd prefers the genitive construction because most leading readers use it and it includes all terror; tanwīn suggests one terror among others.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد الإضافة؛ لأن أكثر الأئمة عليه، ولأنه يعم جميع الفزع

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ also prefers the genitive construction.
rows.anchor: واختار الفراء أيضا الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard reading of ṣanʿa Allāh has ḍamma on ṣād; another reading has fatḥa as a verbal noun, while the ḍamma reading is an initial clause meaning no one can make it.
rows.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة: (صنع الله) بضم الصاد، وقرئ بفتحها، فالفتح على المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard reading says alladhī ḥarramahā, referring to God.
rows.anchor: والقراءة الظاهرة: (الذي حرمها) يعني الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās has the feminine relative pronoun allatī, referring to the town.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: (التي) إشارة إلى البلدة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers use second-person tafʿalūn in “your Lord is not heedless of what you do”; the remaining readers use third-person yafʿalūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب: (وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون) بالتاء

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim takes ṣūr as the plural of ṣūra, “form,” but the author says this is unlikely because its plural would be ṣuwar.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: هذا بعيد، لأن جمع صورة صور بفتح الواو كسورة وسور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horn-like interpretation of ṣūr is that it resembles a trumpet into which Israfil blows.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو يشبه بوق ينفخ فيه إسرافيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dākhir means low and humbled; dakhira describes becoming low, and adkharahu means another humbled him.
rows.anchor: والداخر: الصاغر الذليل، دخر الرجل فهو داخر: إذا ذل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamd denotes freezing or stillness, and by extension little rain, dry land, or a miser.
rows.anchor: والجمد معروف، جمد الماء يجمد، وسنة جماد: قليلة المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabā means casting someone face-down; kabkaba is an object's tumbling into a pit until it settles.
rows.anchor: وكببته لوجهه كبا: ألقيته فقلبته، والكبكبة: تدهور الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm can be accusative by an implied command, “remember the day,” or as an adverb of the preceding event's occurrence.
rows.anchor: يوم) قيل: نصب بمحذوف أي: اذكر يوم، وقيل: نصب على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ṣanʿa Allāh alladhī atqana, ṣanʿ is accusative by the preceding “the mountains pass like clouds,” understood as “God made it”; it may instead be a verbal noun or an exhortation to observe God's work.
rows.anchor: نصب صنع، بما دل عليه ما تقدم من الكلام وهو: (وهي تمر مر السحاب)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to yawm yunfakhu may be implicit in the conjunction, an understood event, or the consequence “when the trumpet is blown, they panic.”
rows.anchor: ويقال: أين جواب: (يوم ينفخ)؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dākhirīn is accusative as a circumstantial expression describing how people are in that state.
rows.anchor: داخرين) نصب على الحال؛ لأن الإنسان يكون هكذا في هذه الحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blower is Israfil, acting by God's command, and the ṣūr is a horn like a trumpet, as Mujāhid and most exegetes say.
rows.anchor: قيل: النافخ إسرافيل بأمر الله في الصور قيل: قرن ينفخ فيه

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Mujāhid and most exegetes understand the ṣūr as a horn into which one blows.
rows.anchor: قرن ينفخ فيه شبه بوق، عن مجاهد وأكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet answered that the ṣūr is a horn into which one blows.
rows.anchor: وروي أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - سئل عن الصور فقال: قرن ينفخ فيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view posits three blasts: terror, swooning, and then rising to the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي ثلاث نفخات: الأولى: نفخة الفزع، والثانية: نفخة الصعق

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatāda, and Abū ʿUbayda explain ṣūr as the forms of created beings into which the spirit is blown for resurrection.
rows.anchor: الصور: صور الخلق؛ يعني: ينفخ الروح في الصور ويبعثون، عن الحسن، وقتادة، وأبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says a tremendous sound emerges, leaving no human heart steady; when they hear it they praise God, and those in heaven and earth panic.
rows.anchor: يخرج منه صوت عظيم لا يثبت معه قلب لبشر، فإذا سمعوا حمدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “Lord of this town” is the Lord of Mecca, who made it a secure sanctuary where hunting, cutting its plants, and retaliation are forbidden.
rows.anchor: رب هده البلدة يعني مكة الذي حرمها يعني جعلها حرما آمنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God made Mecca sacred from contempt and required its veneration.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حرم الاستخفاف بها وأوجب التعظيم لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ownership of everything includes creation and dominion.
rows.anchor: وله كل شيء خلقا وملكا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Being among the Muslims means following the religion of Islam.
rows.anchor: قيل: على دين الإسلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means being among those who submit to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من المنقادين له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting the Quran means reading it to people so they reflect, recognize its miraculous character and religious teachings, and act on its commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: ليتدبروا فيه، ويعلموا كونه معجزة ومعالم دينهم، ويعملوا بأوامره ونواهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided person accepts the truth; the benefit of that guidance returns to the person himself.
rows.anchor: سلك طريقة الهدى بقبول الحق وما جاء فيه فإنما يهتدي لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For one who strays from religion, the Messenger's sole duty is warning, which he has fulfilled.
rows.anchor: ومن ضل عن الدين فقل له: إنما أنا من المنذرين يعني: ليس علي إلا التخويف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet praises God for His blessings; God will show people signs in His religion.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله على نعمه سيريكم آياته في دينه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The signs may be the proofs God sets forth in this world.
rows.anchor: قيل: في الدنيا بما نصب من الأدلة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the signs will appear in the afterlife and compel recognition.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في الآخرة حتى يضطرون إلى المعرفة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the signs will be shown and acceptance will then be up to the people.
rows.anchor: قيل: سيريهم الآيات ثم القبول إليهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The signs may mean the punishment that descends upon them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالآيات العذاب النازل بهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The signs may instead be the portents of the Hour.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أشراط الساعة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the signs with what befell them at Badr.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما نزل بهم يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not unaware of their deeds and will repay them for all of them.
rows.anchor: لا يخفى عليه شيء من ذلك فيجازيهم بجميعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet is blown near the Resurrection; because people use a trumpet to assemble, the same familiar means benefits servants at the gathering.
rows.anchor: وقد جرت العادة بضرب البوق للاجتماع، ففعلوا بهم يومئذ كما اعتادوه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At that time all creation submits, unlike in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن جميع الخلق ينقاد بخلاف الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains will be uprooted, one of the signs of the Hour.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الجبال تقلع، وذلك من أشراط الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He perfected everything” implies that what is corrupt and ugly is not God's making.
rows.anchor: ما كان فاسدا وقبيحا فليس من صنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise and threat show that reward and punishment are recompense for deeds.
rows.anchor: أن الثواب والعقاب جزاء على الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that believers are safe from terror means a believer will not be frightened.
rows.anchor: أن المؤمن لا يفزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinner cast face-first into the Fire shows that a major sinner enters Hell, refuting the Murjiʾa.
rows.anchor: أن صاحب الكبيرة يدخل النار، فيبطل قول المرجئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes Mecca's distinction as a sanctuary and the duty to venerate it.
rows.anchor: وتدل على اختصاص مكة بكونها حرما، وبوجوب تعظيمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is obligated to warn.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن الواجب على الرسول الإنذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses refute the determinists: perfected creation, human deeds, good and evil actions, guidance and error, and divine awareness all assign actions to people and connect them to recompense.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (تفعلون) وقوله: (من جاء بالحسنة)، (ومن جاء بالسيئة)

rows.speaker: جعفر المدني
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Madanī reads yabṭishu with ḍamma on ṭāʾ; the other readers use kasra, and both are dialect forms.
rows.anchor: قرأ جعفر المدني: يبطش بضم الطاء، والباقون بكسرها، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd means strength and bodily vigor; it is a plural of shidda, like niʿma and anʿum.
rows.anchor: الأشد: جمع شدة، مثل نعمة وأنعم، وهي القوة والجلادة في البدن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Ashudd may refer to ages fifteen through forty.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الأشد في خمسة عشر إلى أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wakz can mean pushing, striking with a closed hand, or stabbing; nakaza and lahaza are comparable verbs.
rows.anchor: والوكز: الدفع، والوكز: الضرب بجمع الكف، والوكز: الطعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓahīr means helper, as one becomes like a back to another; ẓuhūr also means dominance.
rows.anchor: والظهير: المعين، وسمي بذلك لأنه يصير كالظهر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taraqqub is waiting; raqīb is a guard or watcher, and marqab is a raised lookout.
rows.anchor: والترقب: الانتظار، والرقيب: الحافظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istisrākh means seeking an outcry for help against an enemy to deter him from attack.
rows.anchor: والاستصراخ: طلب الصراخ على العدو بما يردعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istinṣār means asking for aid.
rows.anchor: والاستنصار: طلب النصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghāwī means immersed in falsehood; taghāwī is people gathering for it.
rows.anchor: والغوي: المنهمك في الباطل، والتغاوي: التجمع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʾtimār means consultation and people consulting each other, as in the cited poetic line.
rows.anchor: والائتمار: المشاورة وأمر بعضهم لبعض، ائتمر القوم وتآمروا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poet says that people have adopted a new custom and deliberate together over every event; the line illustrates consultation.
rows.anchor: أرى الناس قد أحدثوا شيمة ... وفي كل حادثة يؤتمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The killing was not created by God, refuting the determinists: if God created it and the devil prompted it, attribution to the latter would be more fitting.
rows.anchor: أنه لم يكن خلقا لله تعالى فيبطل قول المجبرة؛ لأنه لو خلق فيه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of Satan as a misleader shows God does not mislead: if misguidance were God's creation, Satan would not be called a misleader.
rows.anchor: أن الضلال لو كان خلقا له لما كان الشيطان مضلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second argument is that God censures Satan as a misleader, so God cannot himself mislead.
rows.anchor: أنه ذم الشيطان بأنه مضل فكيف يضل هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' confession that he wronged himself indicates a minor sin and that the act was not created by God.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: (إني ظلمت نفسي) على مواقعة صغيرة، وأنه فعله ليس بخلق لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' pledge not to be a supporter forbids assisting oppressors.
rows.anchor: ويدل قوله: (فلن أكون ظهيرا) أنه لا يجوز معاونة الظلمة

rows.speaker: المجبرة
rows.claim: The determinists object that God created error in people, prevented them from faith, withheld their ability to believe, and created the capacity that necessitates disbelief.
rows.anchor:
القدرة الموجبة للكفر [*].
قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ in where to pause around al-khiyara and in whether mā means “that which”; both analyses are sound.
rows.anchor: للقراء في الوقف في هذه الآية طريقتان: أحدهما: الوقف عند قوله: (الخيرة) و(ما) بمعنى (الذي)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first analysis, God has chosen something, so people cannot choose otherwise.
rows.anchor: فعلى الأول أنه اختار الله شيئا، فليس لهم أن يختاروا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second analysis, God chooses what benefits and serves people's interests.
rows.anchor: وعلى الثاني: إنما يختار مصالح العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAsā and laʿalla are synonymous; when people use ʿasā it expresses hope, while from God it indicates certainty except in the cited exception.
rows.anchor: (عسى) و(لعل) من النظائر، وقيل (عسى) منا بمعنى الرجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiyara means preferring one thing over another, as does ikhtiyār.
rows.anchor: والخيرة: إيثار شيء على غيره، ونظيره: الاختيار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The verse about God's creating and choosing was revealed in response to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra's demand that the Quran be sent to a great man from one of the two towns.
rows.anchor: نزل قوله: (وربك يخلق) الآية. جوابا لقول الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Another report says the verse was revealed after people proposed that God send a different man rather than Muhammad as messenger.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن قوما قالوا: لو أراد رسولا لأرسل فلانا وفلانا دون محمد، فنزلت الآية، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance means regretting past wrong, resolving not to repeat a sin or omit an obligation, and making amends for rights of God and people where possible.
rows.anchor: أن يندم على ما سلف، ويعزم على ألا يعود إلى أمثاله من فعل قبيح أو ترك واجب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Belief with repentance can mean abandoning unbelief.
rows.anchor: قيل: آمن مع التوبة فيقلع من الكفر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means persevering in one's faith.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يثبت على إيمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous action is carrying out what one is commanded to do and refrain from, as directed.
rows.anchor: وعمل صالحا وهو ما كلف فعله وتركه، فيؤديه كما أمر

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī interprets “perhaps he will be among the successful” as “he will be among the successful,” meaning he must attain his aim.
rows.anchor: أي: يكون من المفلحين، عن أبي علي. يعني: لا بد أن ينال الفلاح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The wording ʿasā reflects that entitlement to reward depends on continuing in repentance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما ذكر (عسى)؛ لأن استحقاق الثواب بالدوام على التوبة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says the repentant remains in a state of hope.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأن التائب في حكم الراجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates and chooses by His power over all things, and chooses what is best for people because He knows outcomes.
rows.anchor: وربك يخلق ما يشاء ويختار؛ لأنه القادر على جميع ذلك، ويختار ما هو الأصلح لهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says God chooses whatever He wills and people have no right to select divine affairs for Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يختار ما يشاء ليس لهم تخير الأمور على الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God chooses a suitable person for prophethood; people cannot select, since they do not know who merits it or where benefit lies.
rows.anchor: يختار للنبوة من يصلح لها ليس لهم أن يختاروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorifying God denies any partner in His creation or choice and any error or ugliness in His actions and choices.
rows.anchor: تنزيها له عن شريك في خلقه وفي اختياره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing God's power, the passage establishes His knowledge, since sound choice depends on both.
rows.anchor: لما بين كونه قادرا عقبه ببيان كونه عالما؛ لأن اختيار الأحسن بهما يتم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: God knows hidden thoughts, secrets, and what is openly displayed, and thus chooses a fit person for prophethood.
rows.anchor: يعلم الضمائر والسرائر وما يظهر، فيختار للنبوة من يصلح لها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God knows all things, does what is best for people, and does nothing evil.
rows.anchor: هو العالم بالأشياء فيفعل الأصلح، ولا يفعل القبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is deity and deserves praise in this world and the next because the blessings of both come from Him.
rows.anchor: له الحمد في الأولى أي: الدنيا والآخرة أي: هو يستحق الحمد في الدارين؛ لأن نعم الدارين منه
